sanskrit: sa tvam uttiṣṭha yudhyasva vinīya bhayam ātmanaḥ ghātayitvā sarvasainyaṃ bhrātṝṃś caiva suyodhana
english: So rise up, you, and fight, casting off the fear within you—having destroyed your whole army and your brothers too, O Suyodhana.

sanskrit: nedānīṃ jīvite buddhiḥ kāryā dharmacikīrṣayā kṣatradharmam apāśritya tvadvidhena suyodhana
english: It is no time now to set your mind on life out of a wish to act righteously, O Suyodhana; rather, one of your kind should hold fast to the warrior's duty.

sanskrit: yat tat karṇam upāśritya śakuniṃ cāpi saubalam amartya iva saṃmohāt tvam ātmānaṃ na buddhavān
english: Leaning upon Karṇa and upon Śakuni the son of Subala, you understood not your own self, deluded as though you were immortal.

sanskrit: tat pāpaṃ sumahat kṛtvā pratiyudhyasva bhārata kathaṃ hi tvadvidho mohād rocayeta palāyanam
english: Having wrought that exceedingly great evil, fight back, O Bhārata; for how should one of your kind, out of folly, find flight pleasing?

sanskrit: kva te tat pauruṣaṃ yātaṃ kva ca mānaḥ suyodhana kva ca vikrāntatā yātā kva ca visphūrjitaṃ mahat
english: Where has that manhood of yours gone, and where your pride, O Suyodhana? Where has your valor gone, and where your great thundering boast?

sanskrit: kva te kṛtāstratā yātā kiṃ ca śeṣe jalāśaye sa tvam uttiṣṭha yudhyasva kṣatradharmeṇa bhārata
english: Where has your skill in arms gone, and why do you lie down in this pool of water? Rise up, you, and fight by the warrior's duty, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: asmān vā tvaṃ parājitya praśādhi pṛthivīm imām atha vā nihato 'smābhir bhūmau svapsyasi bhārata
english: Either conquer us and rule this earth, or, slain by us, you shall sleep upon the ground, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: eṣa te prathamo dharmaḥ sṛṣṭo dhātrā mahātmanā taṃ kuruṣva yathātathyaṃ rājā bhava mahāratha
english: This is your foremost duty, ordained by the great-souled Creator; fulfill it truly and become a king, O mighty chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca naitac citraṃ mahārāja yad bhīḥ prāṇinam āviśet na ca prāṇabhayād bhīto vyapayāto 'smi bhārata
english: Duryodhana said: It is no wonder, great king, that fear should enter a living being; yet it is not from fear for my life, O Bhārata, that I withdrew in dread.

sanskrit: arathaś cāniṣaṅgī ca nihataḥ pārṣṇisārathiḥ ekaś cāpy agaṇaḥ saṃkhye pratyāśvāsam arocayam
english: Without a chariot and without a quiver, my flanking driver slain, alone and without a host in the battle, I chose to take a moment's rest.

sanskrit: na prāṇahetor na bhayān na viṣādād viśāṃ pate idam ambhaḥ praviṣṭo 'smi śramāt tv idam anuṣṭhitam
english: Not for the sake of my life, nor from fear, nor from despair, O lord of peoples, have I entered these waters; this I have done out of exhaustion.

sanskrit: tvaṃ cāśvasihi kaunteya ye cāpy anugatās tava aham utthāya vaḥ sarvān pratiyotsyāmi saṃyuge
english: Take rest yourself, O son of Kuntī, and those who follow you; I shall rise and fight you all in the battle.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca āśvastā eva sarve sma ciraṃ tvāṃ mṛgayāmahe tad idānīṃ samuttiṣṭha yudhyasveha suyodhana
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: We are all well rested indeed, and long have we been seeking you; so rise up now and fight here, O Suyodhana.

sanskrit: hatvā vā samare pārthān sphītaṃ rājyam avāpnuhi nihato vā raṇe 'smābhir vīralokam avāpsyasi
english: Either slay the sons of Pṛthā in battle and win a flourishing kingdom, or, slain by us in the fight, you shall attain the world of heroes.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca yadarthaṃ rājyam icchāmi kurūṇāṃ kurunandana ta ime nihatāḥ sarve bhrātaro me janeśvara
english: Duryodhana said: Those for whose sake I desired the kingdom of the Kurus, O delight of the Kurus—they, all my brothers, lie slain, O lord of men.

sanskrit: kṣīṇaratnāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ hatakṣatriyapuṃgavām nābhyutsahāmy ahaṃ bhoktuṃ vidhavām iva yoṣitam
english: This earth, stripped of her jewels, her bull-like warriors slain, I have no heart to enjoy—as one would not a widowed woman.

sanskrit: adyāpi tv aham āśaṃse tvāṃ vijetuṃ yudhiṣṭhira bhaṅktvā pāñcālapāṇḍūnām utsāhaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Yet even now I hope to vanquish you, Yudhiṣṭhira, breaking the spirit of the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: na tv idānīm ahaṃ manye kāryaṃ yuddhena karhi cit droṇe karṇe ca saṃśānte nihate ca pitāmahe
english: But now I think there is no longer any purpose at all in fighting, with Droṇa and Karṇa stilled in death and the grandsire slain.

sanskrit: astv idānīm iyaṃ rājan kevalā pṛthivī tava asahāyo hi ko rājā rājyam icchet praśāsitum
english: Let this whole earth be yours alone now, O king; for what king, bereft of helpers, would wish to rule a kingdom?

sanskrit: suhṛdas tādṛśān hitvā putrān bhrātṝn pitṝn api bhavadbhiś ca hṛte rājye ko nu jīveta mādṛśaḥ
english: Having lost such friends, sons, brothers, and fathers, with the kingdom seized by you, who like me would care to live?

sanskrit: ahaṃ vanaṃ gamiṣyāmi hy ajinaiḥ prativāsitaḥ ratir hi nāsti me rājye hatapakṣasya bhārata
english: I shall go to the forest, clothed in deerskins; for I, whose side has been slain, take no joy in a kingdom, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: hatabāndhavabhūyiṣṭhā hatāśvā hatakuñjarā eṣā te pṛthivī rājan bhuṅkṣvaināṃ vigatajvaraḥ
english: Her kinsmen for the most part slain, her horses slain, her elephants slain—this earth is yours, O king; enjoy her, your fever gone.

sanskrit: vanam eva gamiṣyāmi vasāno mṛgacarmaṇī na hi me nirjitasyāsti jīvite 'dya spṛhā vibho
english: To the forest I shall go, clad in two deerskins; for I, vanquished, have no longing for life this day, O mighty one.

sanskrit: gaccha tvaṃ bhuṅkṣva rājendra pṛthivīṃ nihateśvarām hatayodhāṃ naṣṭaratnāṃ kṣīṇavaprāṃ yathāsukham
english: Go, you, and enjoy the earth at your ease, O lord of kings—her rulers slain, her warriors slain, her jewels lost, her ramparts crumbled.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ārtapralāpān mā tāta salilasthaḥ prabhāṣathāḥ naitan manasi me rājan vāśitaṃ śakuner iva
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Do not, dear sir, standing there in the water, utter the wailings of one in distress; this prattle of yours, like Śakuni's, finds no place in my mind, O king.

sanskrit: yadi cāpi samarthaḥ syās tvaṃ dānāya suyodhana nāham iccheyam avaniṃ tvayā dattāṃ praśāsitum
english: And even were you able to make a gift of it, O Suyodhana, I would not wish to rule an earth bestowed by you.

sanskrit: adharmeṇa na gṛhṇīyāṃ tvayā dattāṃ mahīm imām na hi dharmaḥ smṛto rājan kṣatriyasya pratigrahaḥ
english: By unrighteousness I would not take this earth given by you; for the acceptance of gifts is not held to be the duty of a warrior, O king.

sanskrit: tvayā dattāṃ na ceccheyaṃ pṛthivīm akhilām aham tvāṃ tu yuddhe vinirjitya bhoktāsmi vasudhām imām
english: I would not desire the whole earth given by you; rather, having vanquished you in battle, I shall enjoy this realm.

sanskrit: anīśvaraś ca pṛthivīṃ kathaṃ tvaṃ dātum icchasi tvayeyaṃ pṛthivī rājan kiṃ na dattā tadaiva hi
english: And being no longer her lord, how do you wish to give the earth away? Why, O king, did you not give this earth even then?

sanskrit: dharmato yācamānānāṃ śamārthaṃ ca kulasya naḥ vārṣṇeyaṃ prathamaṃ rājan pratyākhyāya mahābalam
english: When we sought it rightfully, for the sake of peace within our line, you first rebuffed the mighty scion of the Vṛṣṇis, O king.

sanskrit: kim idānīṃ dadāsi tvaṃ ko hi te cittavibhramaḥ abhiyuktas tu ko rājā dātum icched dhi medinīm
english: What now do you give? What madness has seized your mind? For what king, once assailed, would wish to give away the earth?

sanskrit: na tvam adya mahīṃ dātum īśaḥ kauravanandana ācchettuṃ vā balād rājan sa kathaṃ dātum icchasi māṃ tu nirjitya saṃgrāme pālayemāṃ vasuṃdharām
english: You have no power today to give the earth, O delight of the Kurus, nor to wrest her away by force, O king; so how do you wish to give? Vanquish me in battle, then rule this earth.

sanskrit: sūcyagreṇāpi yad bhūmer api dhrīyeta bhārata tanmātram api no mahyaṃ na dadāti purā bhavān
english: Even so much of the land as could be held on the tip of a needle—not even that much would you give us before, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ pṛthivīm etāṃ pradadāsi viśāṃ pate sūcyagraṃ nātyajaḥ pūrvaṃ sa kathaṃ tyajasi kṣitim
english: How then do you give away this whole earth, O lord of peoples? You who once would not yield a needle's point, how do you now relinquish the land?

sanskrit: evam aiśvaryam āsādya praśāsya pṛthivīm imām ko hi mūḍho vyavasyeta śatror dātuṃ vasuṃdharām
english: Having attained such lordship and ruled this earth, what fool would resolve to give the realm to his enemy?

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu kevalamaurkhyeṇa vimūḍho nāvabudhyase pṛthivīṃ dātukāmo 'pi jīvitenādya mokṣyase
english: But you, deluded by sheer folly, do not understand: though you wish to give the earth, this day you shall be parted from your life.

sanskrit: asmān vā tvaṃ parājitya praśādhi pṛthivīm imām atha vā nihato 'smābhir vraja lokān anuttamān
english: Either conquer us and rule this earth, or, slain by us, go to the most exalted worlds.

sanskrit: āvayor jīvato rājan mayi ca tvayi ca dhruvam saṃśayaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vijaye no bhaviṣyati
english: While the two of us yet live, O king—both I and you—a doubt about the victory of either will surely remain among all beings.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ tava duṣprajña mayi saṃprati vartate jīvayeyaṃ tv ahaṃ kāmaṃ na tu tvaṃ jīvituṃ kṣamaḥ
english: Your life, O evil-minded one, rests now in my hands; I could, if I wished, let you live—but you are not fit to live.

sanskrit: dahane hi kṛto yatnas tvayāsmāsu viśeṣataḥ āśīviṣair viṣaiś cāpi jale cāpi praveśanaiḥ tvayā vinikṛtā rājan rājyasya haraṇena ca
english: For you made every effort to burn us, above all, and with venomous serpents, with poisons, and with drownings in water; you wronged us, O king, by the seizure of our kingdom too.

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇāt pāpa jīvitaṃ te na vidyate uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha yudhyasva tat te śreyo bhaviṣyati
english: For this reason, O wicked one, there is no life left for you; rise up, rise up and fight—that shall be the better course for you.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evaṃ tu vividhā vāco jayayuktāḥ punaḥ punaḥ kīrtayanti sma te vīrās tatra tatra janādhipa
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus did those heroes proclaim, again and again, manifold words ringing with victory, here and there, O lord of men.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca evaṃ saṃtarjyamānas tu mama putro mahīpatiḥ prakṛtyā manyumān vīraḥ katham āsīt paraṃtapaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Thus reviled, my son, the lord of the earth, a hero wrathful by nature, a scorcher of foes—how did he bear it?

sanskrit: na hi saṃtarjanā tena śrutapūrvā kadā cana rājabhāvena mānyaś ca sarvalokasya so 'bhavat
english: For never before had he heard such reviling, and through his kingly state he had been honored by all the world.

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca pṛthivī sarvā samlecchāṭavikā bhṛśam prasādād dhriyate yasya pratyakṣaṃ tava saṃjaya
english: And this entire earth, thronged with barbarians and forest dwellers, was upheld by his grace, as you yourself witnessed, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: sa tathā tarjyamānas tu pāṇḍuputrair viśeṣataḥ vihīnaś ca svakair bhṛtyair nirjane cāvṛto bhṛśam
english: He, thus reviled in particular by the sons of Pāṇḍu, bereft of his own servants and wholly hemmed in a desolate place—

sanskrit: śrutvā sa kaṭukā vāco jayayuktāḥ punaḥ punaḥ kim abravīt pāṇḍaveyāṃs tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: hearing those bitter words ringing with victory again and again, what did he say to the Pāṇḍavas? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tarjyamānas tadā rājann udakasthas tavātmajaḥ yudhiṣṭhireṇa rājendra bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitena ha
english: Saṃjaya said: Reviled then, O king, your son standing in the water—reviled by Yudhiṣṭhira together with his brothers, O lord of kings—

sanskrit: śrutvā sa kaṭukā vāco viṣamastho janādhipaḥ dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasya salilasthaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: hearing those bitter words, the lord of men in his dire plight sighed long and hot, again and again, as he stood there in the water.

sanskrit: salilāntargato rājā dhunvan hastau punaḥ punaḥ manaś cakāra yuddhāya rājānaṃ cābhyabhāṣata
english: Submerged within the water, the king, wringing his hands again and again, set his mind upon battle and addressed the king.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ sasuhṛdaḥ pārthāḥ sarve sarathavāhanāḥ aham ekaḥ paridyūno viratho hatavāhanaḥ
english: You, the sons of Pṛthā, are all with your friends, all with your chariots and mounts; I am but one, worn down, chariotless, my mounts slain.

sanskrit: āttaśastrai rathagatair bahubhiḥ parivāritaḥ katham ekaḥ padātiḥ sann aśastro yoddhum utsahe
english: Surrounded by many who bear their weapons and ride their chariots—how, being one man on foot and unarmed, can I dare to fight?

sanskrit: ekaikena tu māṃ yūyaṃ yodhayadhvaṃ yudhiṣṭhira na hy eko bahubhir vīrair nyāyyaṃ yodhayituṃ yudhi
english: But let each of you fight me one by one, O Yudhiṣṭhira; for it is not just that one man should be made to fight against many heroes in battle.

sanskrit: viśeṣato vikavacaḥ śrāntaś cāpaḥ samāśritaḥ bhṛśaṃ vikṣatagātraś ca śrāntavāhanasainikaḥ
english: all the more so when I am without armor, exhausted, taking refuge in the water, my limbs sorely wounded, my mounts and men worn out.

sanskrit: na me tvatto bhayaṃ rājan na ca pārthād vṛkodarāt phalgunād vāsudevād vā pāñcālebhyo 'tha vā punaḥ
english: I have no fear of you, O king, nor of Pārtha, nor of Vṛkodara, nor of Phalguna, nor of Vāsudeva, nor again of the Pāñcālas;

sanskrit: yamābhyāṃ yuyudhānād vā ye cānye tava sainikāḥ ekaḥ sarvān ahaṃ kruddho na tān yoddhum ihotsahe
english: nor of the twins, nor of Yuyudhāna, nor of whatever other warriors you have; alone and enraged, I could well dare to fight them all here.

sanskrit: dharmamūlā satāṃ kīrtir manuṣyāṇāṃ janādhipa dharmaṃ caiveha kīrtiṃ ca pālayan prabravīmy aham
english: The fame of the good among men is rooted in righteousness, O lord of men; guarding both righteousness and renown here, I declare it.

sanskrit: aham utthāya vaḥ sarvān pratiyotsyāmi saṃyuge anvaṃśābhyāgatān sarvān ṛtūn saṃvatsaro yathā
english: I shall rise and fight you all in the battle, meeting each in turn as the year meets all the seasons that come round one after another.

sanskrit: adya vaḥ sarathān sāśvān aśastro viratho 'pi san nakṣatrāṇīva sarvāṇi savitā rātrisaṃkṣaye tejasā nāśayiṣyāmi sthirībhavata pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Today, though unarmed and chariotless, I shall destroy you with your chariots and steeds by my splendor, as the sun at the ebbing of night destroys all the stars; stand firm, O Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: adyānṛṇyaṃ gamiṣyāmi kṣatriyāṇāṃ yaśasvinām bāhlīkadroṇabhīṣmāṇāṃ karṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Today I shall discharge my debt to the illustrious warriors—to Bāhlika, Droṇa, and Bhīṣma, and to the great-souled Karṇa,

sanskrit: jayadrathasya śūrasya bhagadattasya cobhayoḥ madrarājasya śalyasya bhūriśravasa eva ca
english: to brave Jayadratha and to Bhagadatta, to both of them, to Śalya the king of the Madras, and to Bhūriśravas as well,

sanskrit: putrāṇāṃ bharataśreṣṭha śakuneḥ saubalasya ca mitrāṇāṃ suhṛdāṃ caiva bāndhavānāṃ tathaiva ca
english: to my sons, O best of the Bhāratas, and to Śakuni the son of Subala, to my allies and friends and kinsmen likewise.

sanskrit: ānṛṇyam adya gacchāmi hatvā tvāṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ virarāma janādhipaḥ
english: Today I shall discharge my debt by slaying you together with your brothers. Having spoken this much, the lord of men fell silent.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca diṣṭyā tvam api jānīṣe kṣatradharmaṃ suyodhana diṣṭyā te vartate buddhir yuddhāyaiva mahābhuja
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By good fortune you too know the warrior's duty, O Suyodhana; by good fortune your mind turns toward battle alone, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā śūro 'si kauravya diṣṭyā jānāsi saṃgaram yas tvam eko hi naḥ sarvān saṃyuge yoddhum icchasi
english: By good fortune you are a hero, O Kaurava; by good fortune you know warfare, you who, alone, wish to fight us all in the battle.

sanskrit: eka ekena saṃgamya yat te saṃmatam āyudham tat tvam ādāya yudhyasva prekṣakās te vayaṃ sthitāḥ
english: Meeting one against one, whatever weapon is approved by you, take that up and fight; we will stand as your onlookers.

sanskrit: ayam iṣṭaṃ ca te kāmaṃ vīra bhūyo dadāmy aham hatvaikaṃ bhavato rājyaṃ hato vā svargam āpnuhi
english: And this, your cherished wish, O hero, I grant you further: slay any one of us and the kingdom is yours, or, slain, attain heaven.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ekaś ced yoddhum ākrande varo 'dya mama dīyate āyudhānām iyaṃ cāpi vṛtā tvatsaṃmate gadā
english: Duryodhana said: If the choice is granted me this day to fight one in single combat, then of weapons this mace is the one I choose, with your consent.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇāṃ bhavatām ekaḥ śakyaṃ māṃ yo 'bhimanyate padātir gadayā saṃkhye sa yudhyatu mayā saha
english: Whichever one of your brothers thinks he can withstand me, let him fight me in battle on foot with the mace.

sanskrit: vṛttāni rathayuddhāni vicitrāṇi pade pade idam ekaṃ gadāyuddhaṃ bhavatv adyādbhutaṃ mahat
english: Chariot-battles, wondrous at every step, have run their course; let this one great and marvelous mace-duel come to pass today.

sanskrit: annānām api paryāyaṃ kartum icchanti mānavāḥ yuddhānām api paryāyo bhavatv anumate tava
english: Even with their foods do men wish to make a change in turn; let there be a change of battles too, with your assent.

sanskrit: gadayā tvāṃ mahābāho vijeṣyāmi sahānujam pāñcālān sṛñjayāṃś caiva ye cānye tava sainikāḥ
english: With the mace, O mighty-armed one, I shall vanquish you together with your younger brothers, the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas, and whatever other warriors are yours.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha gāndhāre māṃ yodhaya suyodhana eka ekena saṃgamya saṃyuge gadayā balī
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Rise up, rise up, O son of Gāndhārī, and do battle with me, O Suyodhana, meeting one against one in the fight, mace to mace, you mighty one.

sanskrit: puruṣo bhava gāndhāre yudhyasva susamāhitaḥ adya te jīvitaṃ nāsti yady api tvaṃ manojavaḥ
english: Be a man, O son of Gāndhārī, and fight with full resolve; this day there is no life left for you, even were you swift as thought.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etat sa naraśārdūlo nāmṛṣyata tavātmajaḥ salilāntargataḥ śvabhre mahānāga iva śvasan
english: Saṃjaya said: This your son, that tiger among men, could not endure, submerged within the water and hissing like a great serpent in its hole.

sanskrit: tathāsau vākpratodena tudyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ vācaṃ na mamṛṣe dhīmān uttamāśvaḥ kaśām iva
english: Thus goaded again and again by the lash of those words, the wise one could not brook that speech, as a noble steed cannot brook the whip.

sanskrit: saṃkṣobhya salilaṃ vegād gadām ādāya vīryavān adrisāramayīṃ gurvīṃ kāñcanāṅgadabhūṣaṇām antarjalāt samuttasthau nāgendra iva niḥśvasan
english: Churning the water with force, the valorous one took up his mace—heavy, wrought of mountain-iron, adorned with golden bands—and rose up from beneath the water, hissing like the lord of serpents.

sanskrit: sa bhittvā stambhitaṃ toyaṃ skandhe kṛtvāyasīṃ gadām udatiṣṭhata putras te pratapan raśmimān iva
english: Cleaving the spellbound water and laying the iron mace upon his shoulder, your son rose up, blazing like the radiant sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaikyāyasīṃ gurvīṃ jātarūpapariṣkṛtām gadāṃ parāmṛśad dhīmān dhārtarāṣṭro mahābalaḥ
english: Then the wise and mighty son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra grasped the heavy mace of tempered iron, embellished with gold.

sanskrit: gadāhastaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā saśṛṅgam iva parvatam prajānām iva saṃkruddhaṃ śūlapāṇim avasthitam sagado bhārato bhāti pratapan bhāskaro yathā
english: Beholding him mace in hand, like a peaked mountain, standing there like the trident-bearer enraged against his creatures, the Bhārata with his mace shone, blazing like the sun.
